cells.tense: You are handing your strength to the people who need it right now.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, one thing you would aim at if the direction were already settled.
cells.core:
You take what you have and put it where it's needed, and it goes out by measure. Nobody had to haul it out of you. What you hand over lands, and the people around you stand up steadier because of it, though they may not say so.

This runs well when help comes back as light — something you already finished reaches its own end and you get to stand in that for an hour. The bend now is that you keep checking the scale instead of letting the flow move: is this too much, will they expect it again. Put the scale down for one turn.
cells.sheetLine: You give by measure. You just keep checking the scale.
cells.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it

cells.tense: You will be holding everything before anyone has asked you to.
cells.ask: When the fix comes to you today, say not yet once — no apology attached.
cells.core:
The future is the room you're furnishing. Before anyone reaches for it, the thing is already in your hands — the bill covered, the problem half-solved, the worry taken. You call it being reliable. It's a grip that lands ahead of the moment it belongs to.

This holds well when it carries what's actually there without crushing it. The bend is that you're lifting weight that hasn't arrived, and it doesn't get set down, so it doesn't land anywhere. Strength spent early leaves nothing when the real need shows up, and the real need tends to show up on someone else's schedule. The next ask can wait for the ask.
cells.sheetLine: You're lifting things nobody has handed you yet.
cells.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it

cells.tense: You stopped offering your strength back when offering it went where you didn't want.
cells.ask: Pick one person and one thing you can hand over this week, then hand it over and stop.
cells.core:
You've gone quiet with what you have. Your hands are full and the need around you is real, and you let it pass without reaching. There's a door you brought your strength to once, and you don't go near it now.

What this looks like running clean: it holds without forcing, and it starts where you've already finished something, not where you're trying harder. You don't need more endurance for this. The strength is still in your hands; what went quiet is the offer. One small yes, said out loud where someone can see it, is enough to start it moving again.
cells.sheetLine: You have something to give and you've stopped giving it.
cells.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it

cells.tense: You are already shaping what happens next around you, and you're calling it just being helpful.
cells.ask: Name the part of this you're actually doing — out loud, once, to whoever is closest.
cells.core:
Look at how you spent the last few days. Money moved, favors landed, someone got back on their feet — a lot of it had your hands on it. It isn't luck and the room just happens to be okay. You were the one making it, and it won't sit right until you say so.

This runs clean when the shine comes from something that reached its own finish, not from management. Right now you're doing the turning and keeping your hands off the claim. Say out loud that the turn was yours, and what you give stops being a current that passes through and becomes something you chose to hand over.
cells.sheetLine: You're doing the shaping. You just haven't claimed it.
cells.verb: sharing your strength with the people who need it

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: "what you might make" — the record does not say what the person is actually building; the reader could reasonably object that the making was never theirs to begin with, only a thing they were carried through. The ask survives that objection: telling one person, without framing it as a lesson, still stirs authorship in the source even if the finish is later or opinionated. Sentence serving the writer more than the person: "you were the thing being made as much as the one making" — it is neat, and it can vanish from the piece.
